A coral-pink dawn meadow where spider-silk stretches between flower-heads jeweled with dew, early light refracting into tiny scattered rainbows at every turn, the whole field shimmering as the first breeze moves through.
A sunken garden ringed by ancient standing stones draped in flowering moss, soft gold light pooling at its center from an opening in the canopy above, the air thick with warm pollen and old magic.
A sea-cliff bower where wind-twisted trees frame an open view of the glowing ocean below, salt-spray hanging in the air, the cliff edge carpeted in sea-thrift blooming vivid pink against grey stone.
A mist-filled valley at first light, trees emerging as dark silhouettes from white fog, a slow river winding silently through, lantern-moss on every stone glowing amber where the mist is thickest.

A mirror lake at midnight, the surface so still it perfectly doubles every star, tall reeds at the margins silver-tipped with moonlight, a single ancient willow leaning out over the perfect reflection.

A forest of giant ferns in deep emerald shadow, shafts of green-filtered light falling between fronds, tiny luminous insects drifting like sparks, the ground soft with centuries of layered growth underfoot.
An overgrown amphitheatre of pale stone half-swallowed by flowering vines, moonflowers open wide in darkness, their white faces glowing softly, the tiered seats carpeted in thick moss and shadow.

A rivermouth estuary at dusk where the fresh water meets the sea in shifting layers, reed-beds glowing copper in dying light, egrets standing motionless, the whole scene dissolving softly between water and sky.

A cliffside cave mouth draped in hanging gardens, ferns and bell-flowers cascading over stone, fireflies gathered thick at the entrance as if marking a threshold, the cave-dark inside warm and faintly glowing.
A forest glade after rain where every surface holds water, each droplet a tiny lens bending light, the air washed perfectly clear, luminous lichen lit brighter by the wet, the whole clearing jeweled.

A high-mountain plateau of wind-sculpted stone and low flowering heather, aurora-light washing overhead in slow green and violet waves, the stone underfoot veined with mineral that catches and holds the shifting colors.
